**Test Image Observations:**
- **Affected part**: Corn ear with kernels and husks
- **Key features**: 
  - Whitish/pale discoloration of kernels
  - White mold visible on kernels
  - Bleached/whitened husks
  - Kernels appear covered with fungal growth
  - Classic ear rot presentation

This is clearly an ear rot disease. The white fungal growth and bleached husks are the key diagnostic features. Let me examine reference images to identify which specific ear rot variant.

**Analysis of Reference Images:**

| Class | Key Features in Reference | Match to Test? |
|-------|---------------------------|---------|
| **Ear_rots_Diplodia** | White mold on kernels, bleached/whitened husks, grayish-brown kernels | **Perfect match** ✓ |
| Ear_rots_Gibberella | Pinkish-white mold (test shows white), affects ear tip | No - color differs |
| Fusarium | White/pink mold on scattered kernels individually | No - mold is sparse, not covering |
| Ear_rots_Aspergillus | Olive-green powdery mold | No - wrong color |
| Ear_rots_Trichoderma | Dark green mold covering ear | No - wrong color |
| Common_smut | Galls (abnormal growths), not mold | No - wrong disease type |

**Diagnostic Match:**
The test image shows:
- ✓ White fungal mycelium covering kernels
- ✓ Bleached/whitened husks (distinctive indicator)
- ✓ Mold starting from base/covering kernels
- ✓ Pale coloration of affected kernels

This perfectly aligns with Ear_rots_Diplodia's description: "White fungal mycelium growing over and between kernels...Bleached husks while the rest of the plant remains green."
